title: the preflight revert restores changed build files and drops added ones
intention: preflight's build-reverted run reverts every build file to the pre-build commit: a changed file goes back to its pre-build bytes and an added file is removed, so the hollow reading it prints is never falsely green.
why: Measured 2026-11-18 on ticket b7068b1ba431: preflight.sh reverts with `git checkout $PRE -- files || <rm the files absent at $PRE>`. One build file was new, so the checkout failed whole and the fallback only deleted it; verdict.py stayed at HEAD and the reverted run read teeth 1, 2 and 4 green. The hollow had to be taken by hand.
traces_to: Law 8: nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass.
how: New cairn/devices/cc/scripts/revert_build.sh <pre> <files...>, run in the cwd: per file, `git cat-file -e <pre>:<f>` then `git checkout -q <pre> -- <f>`, else `rm -f <f>`. preflight.sh's revert line becomes `bash <scripts>/revert_build.sh $PRE "$@"` inside the worktree. The proof builds a scratch git repo under tmp_path.

measured.saw: with test_a_red_is_re_run_alone.py new and verdict.py changed, preflight's reverted run left verdict.py at HEAD and read teeth 1, 2, 4 green; a hand revert in a worktree read all 5 red
measured.how: preflight.sh verdict 2b73a62f3 <proof> <files> on akiendelllinux, then git checkout per file by hand

constraints: the revert is per file, never one checkout over the whole list
preflight.sh calls revert_build.sh and keeps no inline revert
the proof runs revert_build.sh in a scratch git repo with git -c user.name/user.email, one tooth per outcome

outcomes.claim: over a build that modifies m and adds n, revert_build.sh <pre> m n leaves m at its pre-build bytes
a build that only modifies files is reverted to the pre-build bytes
preflight.sh invokes revert_build.sh for its reverted run and runs no git checkout of its own
